name: Energy Transition Systems

stations.why: A photovoltaic array that is energised whenever the sun is up and cannot be switched off at the panel.
Grid storage: AC before DC, the bleed-down and the thermal event you are trying not to start.
The load end: high-current DC in a public place.
The interconnection, switched on a written order with grounds proven on.
A smaller string in a cabinet, where the same chemistry is maintained by one person alone at night.
Grid storage from delivered to first charge, where the gas detection is proven before the doors are trusted and a cell group running hot is stopped on the E-stop.
The depot row at the panel a whole fleet plugs into: zero energy proven before the lockout, a cut cable and a live ground fault both caught before the vans ever see them.

The corridor these stations feed and draw from, walked and driven on open range, where a downed conductor is treated as energised from the first look at it, not judged safe by what it looks like lying in the grass.
The array itself serviced under a real combiner lockout, with the manual override never turning a row until the meter, not the switch position, says the DC is actually dead.

summary: The plant a utility is building now: solar, storage, charging and the substation that ties them together. Direct current behaves differently, and every station here is about that difference.
union: IBEW outside construction and utility locals
